text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc. made its market debut on the New York Stock Exchange Thursday, creating a sensation at the venerable market by bringing a cow to the trading floor.
The direct marketer of personal computers uses a cow motif on its PC boxes. Gateway's 34-year-old ponytailed founder, Chairman and CEO Ted Waitt, rang the opening bell.
The stock was one of the most active issues on the NYSE, with more than a half a million shares traded within the first half hour of trading. It rose 25 cents to $69.25.
Gateway executives said they toyed with the idea of having MOO as its stock symbol, but settled for GTW instead.

Waitt said the company moved to the NYSE for "trading efficiencies, tighter quotation spreads and greater liquidity in this larger, more stable trading environment. This is an important step toward maximizing long-term value for our individual and institutional investors," he said in a statement.
Gateway 2000 Inc. is based in North Sioux City, S.D.. In 1996, it shipped 1.9 million systems and posted revenues of $5 billion and net income of $250 million.
